lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The Leafs have spent the final preseason days looking less like a team auditioning than one locking the doors behind it - and that is exactly what a contender should do. After a 6-1 thumping of Ottawa and a 4-2 follow-up, Toronto closed its exhibition slate with two clean wins over the Senators, a useful bit of muscle before Tuesday's opener against Montreal. The numbers are simple enough: 4 preseason games, 2 wins, 2 losses. More telling is the posture - Morgan Rielly is being asked to thrive in a different role, and the early signs say he's accepting the assignment with veteran pride. Off the ice, the club's visit to the Mayich family in Arizona showed a roomful of men who still understand the game's human ledger. Now comes the test that matters: Tuesday night, Montreal, and the first real answer.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The season's limp final act has become a quiet showcase - one last chance to see who belongs in the next Blue Jays picture. Toronto dropped Saturday's finale to the Reds 5-1, slipping to 78-83 and 5th in the AL East, with the loss only underscoring how far the club has fallen from contention. Trey Yesavage gave them two innings and a glimpse of the future after his injury-marred year, while Max Scherzer is set for today's finale and still hasn't said whether he'll return. That uncertainty hangs over the room like smoke. Watch Scherzer's start and the younger arms and bats the club gives an audition - because the offseason priorities are obvious: pitching depth, run production, and a cleaner supporting cast around the core.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The new Raptors story is no longer about patience - it's about pressure, and Kawhi Leonard's arrival has put a bright, unforgiving light on everything around him. Leonard's first public turn as a Raptor at media day Monday is the week's most important event, because Bobby Webster has already raised the bar and made clear this isn't a nostalgia act. Toronto opens training camp with a preseason meeting with Miami on Oct. 3 and the real bell on Oct. 21 against Chicago, and that gap is where the shape of this roster gets decided. RJ Barrett and Jakob Poeltl sit right in the middle of the plan, while Scottie Barnes remains the hinge. What matters now is how quickly Toronto can turn all that talent into a clean depth chart before the preseason begins.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The season is wobbling before it has even found its footing - and the blow landed in Dallas, where Jayden Daniels' elbow injury forced Washington back onto Marcus Mariota's broad, aging shoulders. At 0-2 and fourth in the NFC East, two games behind the pace, the Commanders are already chasing the division instead of setting it. The offense flashed only in fragments in the 37-20 loss to the Cowboys, and now the burden shifts to a quarterback who knows the drill but not the ceiling. Daniels is week-to-week, not gone for the year, which is the only comfort here. Mariota starts again today against Seattle, and Washington needs him steady, not cinematic. Watch whether the Commanders can survive the afternoon without turning one injury into a second straight loss.

article.title: Commanders Host Seahawks at 1
paragraphs: The Commanders are at home against the Seahawks today at 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX, with Jayden Daniels out because of an elbow injury and several other regulars also sidelined. Washington comes in 0-2, and the game is at Northwest Stadium in Landover.

For Toronto, the Blue Jays close their season this afternoon against the Reds at 3:07 p.m. ET on Sportsnet, with Max Scherzer set to start in the finale. The Jays fell 5-1 last night, while the Leafs are in Arizona after visiting the Mayich family in hospital before practice and now turn to Tuesday's season opener against the Canadiens. The Raptors are in camp and will play their first preseason game next Saturday against the Heat, before opening the regular season against the Bulls on Oct. 21.
